key_findings.finding: Clinical use is established for detection and treatment of catecholamine-avid tumors, including pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma and neuroblastoma. Clinically recorded toxicity for therapeutic 131I-MIBG is principally radiation- and marrow-related: myelosuppression/cytopenias, with reported nausea/vomiting, fatigue, blood-pressure or heart-rate changes, thyroid injury/hypothyroidism, renal toxicity, and longer-term risk of myelodysplastic syndrome/acute leukemia or other secondary malignancy. The retrieved tools did not provide a primary product-label adverse-event table, so these toxicity details should be verified against the current AZEDRA/iobenguane I-131 prescribing information.
